_about: The prophets' words, taken up later (plan 7.6b): a prophet's words beside the later passages that take them up, each in the passages' own words (Berean Standard Bible, every quotation machine-checked), with Alike and Different in the site's voice. Where a later passage says something 'fulfilled what was spoken', those are its own words, in its cell; the site never says it. Drawn from the Berean editors' own quotation notes (184 into Isaiah-Malachi) and the site's judged links (6.20); rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi (a prophet quoted by another prophet is in this column). Elsewhere in the Old Testament: any other Old Testament book.

rows.title: Be ever hearing, but never understanding

The Prophets: Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving
Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed
Gospels & Acts: You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving
In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled
Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them
they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven
though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand
He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them
You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving
The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet
Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them

rows.alike: Matthew 13:14, Mark 4:12 and Acts 28:26 have Isaiah 6:9's "ever hearing" and "never understanding", "ever seeing" and "never perceiving", and Luke 8:10 has "though seeing" and "though hearing". Matthew 13:15 and Acts 28:27 have Isaiah 6:10's "see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn", and John 12:40 has "see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn".
rows.different: Isaiah 6:9 has "Go and tell this people" and "Be ever hearing" where Matthew 13:14 and Acts 28:26 have "You will be ever hearing"; Mark 4:12 puts seeing first and ends "turn and be forgiven", Isaiah 6:10 ends "turn and be healed", and Matthew 13:15, John 12:40 and Acts 28:27 end "turn, and I would heal them". Matthew 13:14 says "In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled", and Acts 28:25 "The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet".

rows.different: Isaiah 7:14 has "and will call Him Immanuel" and Matthew 1:23 "and they will call Him Immanuel", and Matthew 1:23 goes on "which means, 'God with us'". Isaiah 7:14 opens "Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign", and Matthew 1:22 introduces the words with "All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet". Matthew 1:21 and Luke 1:31 have "you are to give Him the name Jesus".

Luke 3:5-6 has "filled in" where Isaiah 40:4 has "lifted up", and "all humanity will see God's salvation" where Isaiah 40:5 has "the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all humanity together will see it"; Matthew 3:3 says "This is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah".

rows.different: Isaiah 29:13 also has "draw near to Me with their mouths", which Matthew and Mark do not have, and ends "Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men" where they have "They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men".
